correctness.rationale: Each unit chore adds one to load and total share, hence the discrepancies sum to zero, and Prop1 is exactly max discrepancy <=1. An empty bundle has nonpositive discrepancy; a singleton eligibility simply leaves the discrepancy vector unchanged. An independent Fraction-based enumeration on permutation orbits (python /workspace/checks/1.py, output /workspace/checks/1.txt) constructs the closed greedy class for n=1,2,3, checks every entry of the three-agent transition table, and includes every eligible subset and tied choice. Closure starting at zero proves the all-horizon result. At n=4 the depth 0–4 nonsingleton orbit counts 1,3,14,43,87 give labeled counts 1,28,187,617,1405 by permutation multiplicities and maxima 0,3/4,3/4,1,1. Deleting singleton chores transfers this to every four-arrival prefix. In units of 1/12 the adaptive obstruction forces sorted states (-3,-3,-3,9) and (-7,-7,5,9), then either immediate failure with 13 or (-11,1,1,9); choosing the equal pair forces (-11,-5,7,9), then choosing the two positive agents forces a 13 or 15. The all-response minimax calculation independently confirms the first loss at 5 for four agents. For n>=5 two full sets either overload the same recipient or produce two distinct recipients, whose subsequent pair share is 2/n+1/2<1. No n can be forced to fail in two arrivals: use a different recipient when possible; otherwise the first recipient's singleton share alone pays for load minus one. The textual 'self-review' in RESULT.md line 74 is a typo for 'same agent', unambiguous from the stated load and the next sentence. The packaged checker was inspected, not executed.
